title: a richer digital dashboard and a premium wheel centre
lensAText: a sceptical automotive interior art director. Look at every before/after frame the builder cites with the Read tool, then take your own in ONE short Playwright script on dist/artifact.html: the seat view (setCam('cockpit')) of the Rossini GT, the Rossini Corsa and the OC Hypercar at 390x844 (a copy of dist/artifact.html with <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover"> injected; isMobile, hasTouch, DPR 3) at Night and 1280x720 Day, plus one Brio and one Vela E frame. First look at the owner's screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/owner/wheel-dash-v15.png. Judge: does the cluster now show clearly more REAL information, readable at phone size, not hidden by the rim, spokes or hands, honest (simulated values labelled), in each car's style? Does each wheel's centre now read as a premium, stylish, finished part at phone size (sculpted cover, machined bezel, inset badge with a thin accent ring, carbon or brushed insert), in each car's own trim, well made (no gaps, z-fighting, floating parts, the badge crisp, nothing hiding the dials or hands), and OUR OWN design with no real brand's name, logo or copied shape? ALSO (the owner's quality and smoothness ask): drive 60 s in the seat view steering to full lock both ways at 390x844 DPR 3 and watch for any hand or arm clipping, sleeve popping, z-fighting, flicker, shimmer or stutter; check the builder's frame-time table against one short measurement of your own (CDP CPU throttle 4).
brief: THE OWNER (2026-11-11 ~4:05 PM PT), with a phone screenshot of v15's OC Hypercar seat view (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/owner/wheel-dash-v15.png: look at it first): "Make the digital dashboard have more information and make the center of the steering wheel more aesthetic looking". In that screenshot the cluster behind the wheel shows only the OC mark, '49 MPH', a gear box '2' and a partial kW arc, and the wheel's centre is a plain black rounded-square pad with a small OC roundel. TWO PARTS: (A) THE DIGITAL DASHBOARD (the instrument cluster drawn in src/preview/cockpit.ts per car via THEMES and fed by setInstruments from PlayerCar/Game): show MORE REAL information, laid out to stay readable at phone size and not hidden by the wheel's rim, spokes or hands from the seat camera: a tachometer arc with the redline that lights in step with the wheel's shift lights; speed and gear (kept large); the handling profile (Arcade/Sport/Sim/Custom) and TCS/ABS state; trip distance and top speed this run; the game clock and temperature (both simulated: label them honestly, e.g. 'sim'); on the OC Hypercar the Thrust tank and the tune (Unleashed etc.); when Go To has a destination: the next turn arrow with its distance and the destination's name and distance (the same data the HUD uses); a small G-meter or power/regen bar where the car has one. ONLY real game state: never invent fuel, oil, tyre pressure or other values the game does not simulate. Each car keeps its own cluster style (the GT's, the Corsa's, the hypercar's ice-blue, the Brio's and the Vela E's); redraw canvas parts only when a shown value changes (throttled like the dials), no per-frame allocation, a simpler low tier. (B) THE OWNER (2026-10-27, to the hypercar session, now handed to this lane): "make the center part of the steering wheel more stylish". Together with the owner's 2026-11-09 ask for a fresh sport wheel ("looks all fresh like the AMG Alcanatra Carbon Fiber sports steering wheel Mercedes has with the button widgets attached too": our own design in that style family, no real brand names, logos, stars or copied shapes). HEAD is 5cf7212 = the LIVE game v15 (local/live-preview), which already contains the reviewed sport wheel (src/preview/wheel-sport.ts + src/preview/cockpit.ts), the destination HUD fix and the hypercar M1b; claude/sport-wheel was fast-forwarded to it. (B) THE WHEEL CENTRE: BUILD a premium centre (hub/airbag cover) per car, phone-cheap: a sculpted cover (soft-touch leather or Alcantara look matching the car's trim), a machined/brushed bezel ring, the car's own badge inset (R for the Rossinis, V for the Vela E, the OC mark for the hypercar) with a thin accent ring in the car's colour (GT cognac, Corsa yellow, Hypercar ice blue; Brio and Vela in their own accents), and a carbon or brushed insert. The GT, Corsa and Hypercar get the full centre; the Brio and Vela E get a simpler version in their own character. Shared materials, no per-frame allocation, low tier simpler, wheel triangles within the existing budget note (+40% over c3962c5 on high). HARD LIMITS: do NOT change src/preview/spec.ts, hands*, car-wheel.ts, Physics.ts, src/onfoot/people/*; the rim and grips where the hands hold it (GRIP 32/148 deg) unchanged; the dials, thumb pads, paddles and shift lights keep working; nothing else in the cockpit changes. Extend the wheel regression check in tests/regression.mjs to assert the centre's named parts per car. PROVE: npx tsc --noEmit; npm run build (owner-test mark); npm test -- --only=boot,phone (the wheel check inside); seat-view frames Day and Night at 1280x720 and 390x844 for GT, Corsa, Hypercar and one each for Brio and Vela E, plus a close-up of each centre, BEFORE (a9c9998) and AFTER, into tests/out/sport-wheel/hub-*.png. ALSO: the cluster's new content gets a regression assertion (the shown fields follow the game state: gear, profile, Go To next turn) and frames: seat view Day and Night, 390x844 (phone viewport copy, DPR 3) and 1280x720, for the GT and the OC Hypercar with Go To set to Stoppage Time, plus close-ups of each cluster, BEFORE (5cf7212) and AFTER, into tests/out/sport-wheel/dash-*.png. THE OWNER (2026-11-11 ~5:45 PM PT): "make sure graphics are insane for both the steering wheel and characters and make sure it doesn't have any laggy graphics or act glitchy when 1st person POV with the arms and stuff". So: (a) TOP visual quality on HD and Ultra (physically based materials with real detail: stitching, Alcantara nap, carbon weave under clear coat, brushed and machined metal, crisp emissive lines; for people: skin shading, hair shapes, cloth folds and fabric) while Low stays cheap for phones; (b) the FIRST-PERSON views with the arms (the driving seat view, and any first-person on-foot view) must be smooth and glitch-free: no hand or arm clipping through the rim, spokes or centre while steering to full lock both ways, no sleeve or wrist popping, no z-fighting or flicker on the wheel, centre or cluster, no LOD popping in view, no texture shimmer (mipmaps, anisotropy), no per-frame allocation. MEASURE IT: a 120 s seat-view drive with steering, on the phone profile (390x844, DPR 3, isMobile, Chrome DevTools Protocol Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate 4) and on desktop 1280x720: report p50/p95/p99 frame time, long tasks over 50 ms, draw calls and triangles (window.__game stats or renderer.info) and the JS heap at start and end; the same on the base under the same conditions; the result must be no worse than +10 % p95 frame time and show no heap growth; fix any regression at its source. Put the table in the progress entry.
